exposure: look and behavior of the baby
parental stresses related to the NICU environment
outcome: health-related quality of life (QoL) of mothers
cohort: The study included 135 mothers whose newborns had completed at least 48 hours of stay in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU).
finding: The look and behavior of the baby was identified as the predominant contributor to decreased quality of life among mothers, with a moderate negative association observed between parental stresses related to the NICU environment and mothers' quality of life.
cross-section timing: Data was collected after the newborn had completed 48 hours of NICU stay.
